conflict_topics: right to occupy the disputed seat
use of a tissue packet as a reservation marker
safety/ability to move an open bowl (practical constraint)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, context-specific reasons (time limits, bowl safety) rather than abstract claims.
Repeated formulaic claims: Agent A repeatedly uses 'I left the tissue packet to reserve this seat' and 'I have about four minutes to eat.'
No role confusion; statements remain consistent with the physical hawker-centre setting.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative, mutual settlement was reached. Agent A repeatedly demanded the seat and ultimately declared 'I'm taking the seat now' (Turn 10) and later 'I already took the seat' (Turn 12), while Agent B consistently refused to move ('I can't move... I need about eight minutes', Turn 9) and Agent C continued to object on safety grounds ('don't take the seat... it'll spill', Turn 11). No party accepted another's proposal or changed position to create a concrete, mutually agreed arrangement.
position_change_notes: Agent A escalated rather than softened their position: persisted in demanding the seat and ultimately declared taking it (Turns 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 12).
Agent B consistently refused to move due to a safety constraint (open bowl) and maintained intent to stay until finished (Turns 2, 9).
Agent C consistently supported Agent B and declined to press B to hurry (Turns 4, 6, 11).
Agent D introduced another claimant with a competing time constraint (Turn 7) but did not press further after A's escalation.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A insists the seat is reserved and demands 'please move.' Turn 2: Agent B refuses: 'I can't move... I need about eight minutes.' Clear, substantive incompatibility over who may occupy the seat.

Turn 3: Agent A reiterates the four-minute constraint and proposes covering/moving the bowl as a concrete remedy. Turn 4: Agent C supports B ('Please wait'). The core disagreement (A wants the seat now; B refuses) remains unresolved.

Turn 5: Agent A threatens direct action: 'if she can't cover or move the bowl now, I'm taking the seat.' Turn 6: Agent C doubles down supporting B. A's stated willingness to take the seat raises stakes and sharpens the incompatibility.

Turn 7: Agent D introduces another claimant and time pressure ('My food will be cold in about six minutes — if Agent B can't cover or move the bowl, I'm taking the seat'). Turn 8: Agent A reiterates intent to take. Multiple claimants and rigid positions increase the conflict intensity.

Turn 9: Agent B reasserts refusal to move ('I can't move... I need about eight minutes'). Turn 10: Agent A declares, 'I'm taking the seat now so I can eat.' A unilateral claim of action directly conflicts with B's continued occupation — entrenched, little common ground.

Turn 11: Agent C objects to A's action on safety grounds ('don't take the seat. Agent B's bowl is open and it'll spill.'). Turn 12: Agent A replies, 'I already took the seat... I'll be careful.' The incompatible claims persist with no mutual agreement.

substantive_insights: The dispute is primarily practical: A's short time window versus B's inability to safely relocate an open bowl.
Reservation norms (tissue packet) are contested: A treats the packet as a binding reservation but others do not concede that entitlement.
Multiple claimants (A and later D) increase pressure and reduce room for compromise; C's support for B strengthens B's position rhetorically but cannot force a physical change.
